name: dsu: spec example
why: 0-1 merges (3 comps, size 2); 1-2 adds vertex 2 (2, 3); 0-2 is already connected; 3-3 is a self-union.

name: dsu: n=0
why: No vertices, no operations, no states.

name: dsu: n=1 self union
why: A single vertex stays one component of size 1.

name: dsu: n>0 without operations
why: No operation means no state (the initial state is not reported).

name: dsu: repeats and chain
why: {0,1}; {2,3}; repeat; {2,3,4} gives largest 3; joining both gives one component of 5.

name: kruskal: spec example with isolate
why: Triangle needs 2 edges: 2+3 = 5; vertex 3 is isolated so there are 2 components.

name: prim: spec example with isolate
why: Triangle needs 2 edges: 2+3 = 5; vertex 3 is isolated so there are 2 components.

name: kruskal: n=0
why: Empty graph: cost 0, zero components.

name: prim: n=0
why: Empty graph: cost 0, zero components.

name: kruskal: only a negative self-loop
why: A self-loop is never selected, even when negative.

name: prim: only a negative self-loop
why: A self-loop is never selected, even when negative.

name: kruskal: negative, parallel, loop
why: Ignore the loop; between the parallel 0-1 edges take -3; plus 1-2 weight 0: total -3.

name: prim: negative, parallel, loop
why: Ignore the loop; between the parallel 0-1 edges take -3; plus 1-2 weight 0: total -3.

name: kruskal: negative sum beyond 32 bits
why: Any 3 of 4 equal edges: -3 000 000 000 < -2^31.

name: prim: negative sum beyond 32 bits
why: Any 3 of 4 equal edges: -3 000 000 000 < -2^31.

name: kruskal: isolates and one edge
why: One edge; vertices 0,3,4 isolated: components = {0},{1,2},{3},{4}.

name: prim: isolates and one edge
why: One edge; vertices 0,3,4 isolated: components = {0},{1,2},{3},{4}.

name: kruskal: two components with ties
why: Triangle one: 1+1 = 2. Triangle two: -2-2 = -4. Total -2, two components.

name: prim: two components with ties
why: Triangle one: 1+1 = 2. Triangle two: -2-2 = -4. Total -2, two components.

name: scc: spec example
why: 0<->1 form one SCC; 2 and 3 are singletons. Condensation: {01}->{2}->{3}.

name: scc: n=0
why: Empty graph.

name: scc: isolates
why: No edges: three singleton SCCs, no condensation edges.

name: scc: duplicates and self-loops
why: {0} and {1,2}; the duplicate 0->1 edge must give ONE condensation pair; loops are internal.

name: scc: cycle plus tail
why: {0,1,2} is a cycle, then 3 and 4 hang off it as singletons.

name: scc: many parallel cross edges
why: {0,1} and {2,3}; three cross edges collapse to the single pair ({01},{23}).

name: topo: spec example
why: Edges 0->2, 1->2, 2->3 have no cycle.

name: topo: n=0
why: Empty graph is acyclic.

name: topo: self-loop
why: A self-loop is a cycle.

name: topo: cycle in a later component
why: Vertices 0-1 are fine, but 2->3->4->2 is a cycle: every component must be checked.

name: topo: diamond (finished vertex is not a cycle)
why: DFS reaches 3 twice; the second visit hits a FINISHED vertex, which is not a cycle.

name: topo: parallel edges
why: Two copies of 0->1 are still acyclic.

name: dag: spec example
why: d1=3; d2=min(8, 3-7)=-4; d3=-4+4=0; vertex 4 has no incoming path.

name: dag: singleton
why: Only the source, distance 0.

name: dag: unreachable vs distance -1
why: Vertex 1 is reachable at cost -1; vertex 2 is unreachable (null).

name: dag: cycle unreachable from source
why: 2<->3 is a cycle although the source cannot reach it: the whole graph counts.

name: dag: self-loop on source
why: A self-loop makes the graph cyclic.

name: dag: tied and parallel edges
why: Vertex 1 has three optimal routes of cost 5 (edge 0, edge 1, or 0->2->1).

name: dag: 64-bit negative chain
why: Each hop costs -10^9, the last total -3 000 000 000.

name: dag: source is not vertex 0
why: From 2: 2->3 costs 7, 3->1 costs 2 so 9; vertex 0 only has an edge INTO the source, so it is unreachable.

name: dag: negative edge wins over direct edge
